key_insight: A genomic foundation model (Evo2) extracted from tumor variant sequence context added prognostic information beyond established clinicopathologic and transcriptomic sarcoma risk models.
clinical_relevance: In soft tissue sarcoma, sequence-aware genomic features may help refine survival risk stratification when combined with existing models like SARCULATOR and CINSARC.
method: Analyzed FFPE tumor samples and clinical data from 102 sarcoma patients, with 129 TCGA-SARC cases used for external validation.
Converted reconstructable short variants, fusions, and rearrangements into sequence inputs and embedded them with Evo2 to create patient-level representations.
Compared Cox model performance for Evo2 alone and in combination with SARCULATOR or CINSARC across multiple survival endpoints using C-index.
evidence_signal: Reported C-index improvements were seen after adding Evo2, including OS from 0.620 to 0.770 in the study cohort and from 0.595 to 0.716 in TCGA-SARC, with similar gains for other survival endpoints.
watch_item: These are descriptive point-estimate comparisons from retrospective cohorts, so clinical utility and generalizability still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Genomic foundation models extend clinicopathologic and transcriptomic prognostication in soft tissue sarcoma
